title: Affine-space trivialization over the split reductive quotient
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A reductive group means a smooth affine group of finite type, geometrically connected, whose extension to an algebraic closure has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology, def-sfb-solvable-group-structure]. A split maximal torus means a maximal torus isomorphic over the ground field to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$ [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. There exist a reductive $k$-group $H$ having a split maximal torus, a $k$-group homomorphism $q:G\to H$, an integer $n\geq0$, and an isomorphism of $k$-schemes $$a:G\xrightarrow{\sim}H\times_k\mathbf A^n_k,\qquad \operatorname{pr}_H\circ a=q$$ [def-sbc-affine-space, def-pc-fibre-product]. For every field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], $H_L$ is smooth affine and geometrically integral of finite type over $L$, and the scalar extension $a_L:G_L\xrightarrow{\sim}H_L\times_L\mathbf A^n_L$ is an isomorphism over $H_L$ with projection $q_L$. Geometrically integral means nonempty and integral after every field extension; integral means reduced and irreducible. The case $G=1$, with $H=1$ and $n=0$, is included.

source.place: Brion Lemma 2.3 proof, printed p.118, first three sentences (unipotent radical, affine-space variety and trivial torsor); Remark 2.2(v), p.117, for splitting over an algebraically closed field. Geometric integrality of a connected smooth algebraic group is included explicitly as a structural prerequisite.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-unipotent-radical-existence] choose the largest smooth connected closed normal unipotent subgroup $U\subseteq G$. The identity of $G$ is a $k$-rational point, so [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] makes $G$ geometrically connected. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] to obtain $q:G\to H=G/U$: $H$ is smooth affine geometrically connected of finite type, $q$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented, and $(g,u)\mapsto(g,gu)$ identifies $G\times U$ with $G\times_HG$.

If $V\subseteq H$ is a smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] gives its inverse image $P=q^{-1}(V)$ as a smooth connected normal closed subgroup of $G$ in an exact sequence $1\to U\to P\to V\to1$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-unipotent-extension], $P$ is unipotent. Maximality of $U$ therefore gives $P\subseteq U$, and the reverse inclusion is automatic. Thus $P=U$, so its faithfully flat quotient $V=P/U$ is trivial. As $k$ is algebraically closed this is precisely reductivity of $H$. Apply the existence clause of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] to choose a split maximal torus of $H$.

An algebraically closed field is perfect: every algebraic extension has all its elements in $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-perfect-unipotent-additive-series] to $U$ and write its resulting series as $U=U_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq U_m=1$, with smooth connected affine terms and additive quotients. Every tail is a split series of the kind in [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors].

Construct scheme isomorphisms $b_j:U_j\simeq\mathbf A_k^{m-j}$ by reverse induction. For $j=m$ use $U_m=1=\mathbf A_k^0$. Given the construction at $j+1$, [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] makes $U_j\to U_j/U_{j+1}\simeq\mathbf G_a=\mathbf A_k^1$ a represented right $U_{j+1}$-torsor. Its base is affine of finite type and $U_{j+1}$ has the tail split series, so [lem-sfb-split-unipotent-affine-torsor-section] supplies a section $s_j$. The map $(x,v)\mapsto s_j(x)v$ is an isomorphism $\mathbf A_k^1\times U_{j+1}\to U_j$: its inverse takes $y$ to its quotient image $x$ and the unique $v$ in the torsor comparison with $s_j(x)v=y$. This inverse is a morphism by the torsor comparison isomorphism. Compose with $b_{j+1}$ and identify the product with $\mathbf A_k^{m-j}$ by adjoining the coordinate $x$. At $j=0$ put $n=m$ and $b=b_0$.

source.place: Corollary 16.56, p.344, induction on the additive series, using Proposition 16.55(b).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-unipotent-affine-torsor-section] to $q:G\to H$, using the affine finite-type base $H$ and the split series of $U$. Choose an $H$-section $s:H\to G$. The torsor comparison from [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] makes $(h,u)\mapsto s(h)u$ an isomorphism $H\times U\to G$. Its inverse is $g\mapsto(q(g),u(g))$, where the second coordinate is the regular morphism determined by $s(q(g))u(g)=g$. Define $a(g)=(q(g),b(u(g)))$. The displayed inverse and $b^{-1}$ show that $a:G\simeq H\times\mathbf A_k^n$ is a scheme isomorphism, and its first coordinate gives $\operatorname{pr}_H\circ a=q$.

source.place: Proposition 16.55(b) and Corollary 16.56, p.344; Brion Lemma 2.3 uses exactly this torsor trivialization.

proof.text: For the structural clause, apply [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality] to $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. It is smooth by step 1. Its single fibre $H$ is connected and nonempty: $q$ is faithfully flat, hence surjective, so $H=q(G)$ is the continuous image of the connected scheme $G$, and the identity is a point. The identity $e_H:\operatorname{Spec}k\to H$ is a section of the structure morphism, so [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] makes $H_K$ connected for every field extension $K/k$; this is the geometric connectedness (connected after every field extension) required by the next citation (step 1 gave it only after extension to an algebraic closure). The cited statement says that $H_M$ is integral for every field extension $M/k$. In particular, for $L/k$ and every $M/L$, apply it to $M/k$ and identify $(H_L)_M=H_M$ by the fibre-product universal property. This proves geometric integrality of $H_L$, with nonemptiness again witnessed by the identity. Smoothness of $H_L/L$ follows from [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). If $H=\operatorname{Spec}A$, then $H_L=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kL)$ is affine; finite generators of $A$ as a $k$-algebra give generators of $A\otimes_k L$ as an $L$-algebra, proving finite type.

source.place: Proposition 1.62, p.24, with the smooth geometrically connected fibre integrality criterion (Stacks 056T/057J).

proof.text: Pull back $a$ and its inverse along $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Functoriality preserves their two inverse equations and $\operatorname{pr}_H\circ a=q$. The coordinate-algebra identity $k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\otimes_k L=L[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ and the fibre-product universal property identify the pulled-back codomain with $H_L\times_L\mathbf A_L^n$. Thus the pulled-back isomorphism is the required $a_L$ over $H_L$, with first projection $q_L$, without any separability or algebraicity assumption on $L/k$. For $G=1$, choose the length-zero series, $H=1$, $n=0$, $q=\operatorname{id}$ and the canonical product isomorphism.

source.place: Section 1(e), p.24, base change; Corollary 16.56, p.344, length-zero case.

proof_origin.place: Sections 6.45--6.46; Corollary 16.24; Proposition 16.55(b) and Corollary 16.56. Assembly following Brion Lemma 2.3, printed p.118, read online because its PDF is absent locally.

tool_uses.why: The group identity is a rational section, so connectedness becomes geometric connectedness before forming the quotient.
